properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 by reading identity sidecars only, never opening a store. Seven reflow2 designs under ~/project carry an identity file. TWO OF THEM ANSWER TO THE SAME NAME:

  ~/project/reflow2/.reflow2/graph.id.json        graph_id "reflow2"  label "reflow2"        origin adopted
  ~/project/dev_storyflow/.reflow2/graph.id.json  graph_id "reflow2"  label "dev_storyflow"  origin adopted

Both are real, both populated, and the collision has stood since 0.14.0.

⭐ THE CAUSE IS NOT A BUG IN THE ADOPT PATH, and a first diagnosis that said so was wrong. `identity::resolve` adopts THE OLD SHARED DEFAULT ID when a store already holds design data under it — not the project name, not the path. Every graph used one constant before `cap:design-identity` landed, so EVERY PRE-IDENTITY STORE SERVED BY THIS BINARY ADOPTED THE SAME STRING. Two such stores therefore collide BY CONSTRUCTION, and n of them would give n.

AND THE ADOPTION WAS RIGHT. identity.rs states the alternative plainly: minting a fresh id for a populated store would be "a catastrophe of exactly the silent kind — the design would still be on disk, and reflow2 would open a new empty one beside it and report nothing wrong." `graph_id` is also part of the export's content hash, so adoption is what kept every existing export, chain link and committed record valid across the change. The migration chose correctly; the collision is its unpriced consequence.

EVIDENCE THAT MINTING IS CLEAN: the four `minted` designs on this machine — brainmaker 683f0090c245a5f1, flo2 1a97fc1f1de4d5d2, music_graph 4a496c576800020c, quantum_benchmarking_initiative ff86353849198623 — have zero collisions. `mint()` seeds fnv1a with nanoseconds, pid and canonical path, so it is unique by construction. Only the adopted ones collide, and `dynograph-foundation` escapes only because its own codebase carried a different default constant.

🛑 WHY IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN IN 0.14.0: `registry.rs` (2026-08-12) makes `graph_id` the KEY a session selects a design by — `rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` calls the id primary and the path a storage detail. `Registry::discover` accumulates into a `BTreeMap<String, String>` keyed on it, so a second design under the same id does not collide, warn or fail — IT OVERWRITES, and which one survives is decided by alphabetical order of the very path the id exists to hide. Demonstrated in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/two_designs_can_share_one_id.rs: the registry reports 1 design where 2 exist, and `attach("reflow2")` binds to whichever sorted last while the other is unreachable by its own name.

⇒ So a defect that was harmless while ids were only labels became load-bearing the moment ids became addresses. Nothing enforces or checks graph_id uniqueness anywhere.

THE ASYMMETRY WORTH KEEPING: reflow2 is careful about id collisions ONE LEVEL DOWN and has nothing one level up. `mirror_surface` refuses a colliding NODE id and leaves the local node untouched, on the stated ground that "two designs using one id for different things is a naming conversation between their owners." The same hazard between two DESIGNS is a silent overwrite.
